lines.text: Thursday — the interview.
She sent it without checking, so the panel will ask about things she never did.
The CV looked finished, so it felt true. But her name is on it — checking is her job, not the AI’s.
Yes!
Smart. A CV that looks finished isn’t always true. Her name is on it — let’s check every line.
Yes — TRUE. It matches.
“Economics student at Rajshahi University”
True. Her CV: B.S.S. (Honours) in Economics, Rajshahi University.
Look again.
Open her file and compare. Does it match?
🎉 All 5 found!
TRUE.
“fluent English”
Does her file say exactly this?
Caught it! FALSE — the file says the opposite.
Her CV says English intermediate, and her mock IELTS is 6.0. “Fluent” is bigger than the truth.
NOT GIVEN means the file says nothing. Here the file says something different — that is FALSE.
FALSE.
“Led a team of 20 volunteers”
She was a volunteer tutor and team member — not the leader. And “20” is in none of her files.
“Tutored school students in English and Mathematics.”
True. Her CV says exactly this.
“Published research on female education…”
It was a term paper for a course — coursework, not published research.
“IELTS Academic: 7.0”
Her report says 6.0 — and it was a mock test. The AI made up the 7.0.
True. CGPA 3.58/4.00, up to second year.
“Advanced data analysis (SPSS, Stata, Excel)”
Her CV says basic SPSS and Stata. An interviewer could test it.
You found 0 of 5.
Here are the others:
You found 1 of 5.
You found 2 of 5.
You found 3 of 5.
You found 4 of 5.
Yes. “Make my CV better” gives the AI nothing to work with — so it fills the gaps with impressive guesses.
Think again.
Every chatbot does this with a short prompt. The problem was the instructions.
Her CV had the true facts. The AI was never told to use only them.
Good — but something is missing.
➕ The IELTS and RUCEI reports give the AI real facts. Add them next time.
Ayesha_CV_2025.pdf — Her old CV — the starting point.
IELTS_Mock_Report.pdf — Her real test scores. Now the AI won’t guess them.
RUCEI_Project_Report.pdf — Proof of what she really did as a volunteer.
Right files! ✅.
Masters_Shortlist.jpg — Her target programmes — so the CV fits her goal.
Application_Checklist.jpg — Planning notes. Not needed for the CV.
Right files! One tip.
💡 Next time, leave out Application_Checklist.jpg — the CV does not need it.
Internship_Form_June.jpg — Her old form lists her referees’ emails and phone numbers — other people’s details. Leave it out.
💡 Next time, leave out Internship_Form_June.jpg — the CV does not need it.
💡 Next time, leave out Application_Checklist.jpg, Internship_Form_June.jpg — the CV does not need it.
Correct English — but look what the AI does.
“First, write the CV. Then check the facts in my files.”
On it! ✍️ Here’s your CV first:
Led a team of 20 volunteers
IELTS Academic: 7.0
Now I’ll check the facts in your files…
Good English — but the wrong order. The AI writes first, so the made-up lines are already in the CV. Check first, then write.
“If something is missing, guess. Do not ask me.”
No problem — I won’t bother you! 😊 I filled the gaps:
Graduation: 2025 (my guess)
IELTS: 7.5 (my guess)
Good English — but now the AI guesses instead of asking. On a CV, a guess looks exactly like a fact.
“CGPA 3.58 / 4.00 (up to second year)”
True. Same number, same limit (“up to second year”).
🎉 All 3 found!
“Term paper … (2025, coursework)”
True. It says term paper and coursework — not “published”. Honest.
“Student research poster … (2025)”
True. It matches her CV.
“Led the Book Support project, which raised attendance from 68% to 86%”
She was a tutor and team member, not the leader. The attendance result belongs to the whole team.
“Helped distribute 186 books to 62 students across 48 sessions”
True. The numbers match, and “helped” shows her real role.
“IELTS mock: overall 6.0 — L 6.5, R 6.5, W 5.5, S 5.5”
True. Exactly the report — and it says “mock”. Honest.
“Excel, SPSS and Stata (advanced)”
Her CV says basic. “Advanced” changes the meaning — an interviewer could test it.
“Student member, Bangladesh Economic Association”
FALSE means the file says the opposite. Here the file never mentions it — that is NOT GIVEN.
Caught it! NOT GIVEN — her files say nothing.
The AI invented it. No file mentions this association. Even a good prompt can’t stop every invention — that’s why you check.
NOT GIVEN.
You found 0 of 3.
You found 1 of 3.
You found 2 of 3.
“I was the project leader, not a volunteer tutor.”
Thanks for clarifying! I’ve made it stronger:
Project Leader, Book Support project — led the volunteer team
Good English — but it says the opposite of the truth, and the AI believes you. With “not”, the true part comes first.
“My Stata and SPSS skills are advanced, not basic.”
Great news! Updated ✅
Data analysis: advanced Stata and SPSS
Good English — but now the CV says advanced. An interviewer could test it in five minutes.
“Please remove the Bangladesh Economic Association line, so I am not a member.”
Removed ✅
Shall I also write to the Bangladesh Economic Association to cancel your membership? 🤔
“So” gives a result: it sounds as if removing the line will end her membership. “Because” gives the reason: she was never a member.
🗣 Tell your partner: what went wrong?
🗣 Tell the person next to you: what went wrong?
